questions.q: What job does Where-Object do in a pipeline?
options: Filters which whole objects continue, based on a condition — a yes/no per object, unchanged either way
Removes properties from every object that passes through
Runs an action against every object, such as writing to the screen
Sorts objects by a chosen property
questions.explain: Where-Object decides per object whether it continues down the pipeline; it doesn't reshape what passes.

questions.q: What does Select-Object -First 5 do, as opposed to Where-Object?
options: Limits how many objects pass through, without asking whether each object meets any condition
Filters objects based on whether a property equals a specific value
Deletes the first 5 objects and keeps the rest
Runs a script block against each of the first 5 objects
questions.explain: Select-Object narrows properties or row count; it doesn't evaluate a per-object condition the way Where-Object does.

questions.q: What is ForEach-Object typically used for?
options: Running an action against every object that arrives, often for a side effect like writing output
Filtering out objects that don't meet a condition
Choosing which properties an object keeps
Sorting objects in ascending or descending order
questions.explain: ForEach-Object runs code per object, one at a time — it's for doing something to each item, not narrowing the list.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what question helps you pick the right cmdlet among the three?
options: Am I deciding which objects survive, what they look like once they survive, or doing something to each one?
Is the pipeline longer than three stages?
Does the cmdlet name start with the letter S?
Is the data coming from a file instead of a live command?
questions.explain: That single question maps directly onto the three distinct jobs: Where-Object, Select-Object, and ForEach-Object.

questions.q: In Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.CPU -gt 100} | Select-Object Name, CPU | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ... }, what is the correct order of jobs?
options: Filter first, then shape which properties remain, then act on each remaining object
Act on each object first, then filter, then shape
Shape the properties first, then act, then filter
All three stages run simultaneously in no particular order
questions.explain: The pipeline filters with Where-Object, shapes with Select-Object, then acts with ForEach-Object, read left to right.
